title: Responses degradation simulator and heuristic reconciler for OpenAI Responses parity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we migrate workloads to the OpenAI Responses compatibility layer, we observe non-deterministic behavior surface in streaming boundaries, tool/function-call events, and structured-output failure modes. These mismatches cause customer-visible regressions (malformed functioncall payloads, missing finalization events in streams, and divergent structured JSON output). There is no reliable way today to reproduce these failure modes locally or score their severity against Redwood fallbacks.

Objective: Build a deterministic 'degradation simulator' plus a heuristic reconciler component to (1) emulate common OpenAI Responses divergences under configurable conditions, (2) run scoring experiments that quantify parity gap impact on downstream apps, and (3) derive runtime selection heuristics (fallback to variant-model, bridge-shim, or strict schema enforcement) driven by the score.

Scope: This ticket covers a minimal viable simulator and reconciler prototype with: input workload generator, event morphers (stream truncation, out-of-order events, toolcall-parameter mutation, JSON-structure drift), concordance scoring, and an integration hook into the runtime's adaptive routing layer for experiment-only canaries. Production rollout and UI surfaces are out of scope for this ticket and will be tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Simulator can replay a saved conversation and produce at least five configurable degradation modes (stream-trim, delayed-final, toolcall-lost-args, toolcall-extra-keys, structured-field-shift).
2) Concordance score defined and implemented (range 0-100) with unit tests and example thresholds.
3) Heuristic reconciler outputs a ranked set of remediation actions (model-variant, shim-transform, enforce-parse-fallback) for a given degraded trace.
4) End-to-end smoke test demonstrating reconciler recommending a fallback and the runtime applying the fallback on a 1% canary route.
5) Telemetry emitted for all simulated events and reconciliation decisions (see metrics list).
tasks: Design simulator data model and loss primitives
Implement event morphers and replay harness
Create concordance scoring library and tests
Integrate reconciler into runtime canary hook
End-to-end smoke + CI tests and artifacts
milestones: M1: simulator prototype and unit tests (2026-03-07)
M2: reconciler rule engine and scoring (2026-03-14)
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Simulator false-positives cause unnecessary fallback, increasing latency/cost. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and canary-only application until precision validated.
Risk: Reconciler complexity sprawl. Mitigation: rule-skeleton + metrics-first approach and limit initial rule set to three remediation actions.
Risk: Missing corner cases for rare toolcall patterns. Mitigation: collect post-canary telemetry and add prioritized patterns to simulator corpus.
testing_plan: Unit tests for each morphing primitive, fuzz tests against 10k historical traces pulled from anonymized infra dataset, e2e canary with 1% traffic for 48 hours against two sample integrations (chat-with-tool and structured-json-output), and synthetic downstream consumer checks that validate parse success and toolcall parameter fidelity.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged rollouts (off by default). 2) Internal alpha: run simulator offline and compare scores vs known incidents. 3) Controlled canary: 1% traffic in staging -> 1% in prod for partner account cohort. 4) Expand to 10% and then fully on after 2 weeks of stability. All rollouts reversible with immediate toggle.
outstanding_questions: What concordance thresholds should trigger auto-fallback vs alert-only?
Should reconciler rules be expressible in a simple DSL or JSON config?
Do we centralize the simulator corpus or allow per-customer recordings?

notes: This ticket intentionally produces reproducible degradation traces to help quantify parity trade-offs and inform both short-term runtime fallbacks and longer-term protocol mappings. The simulator will also be used as a test harness for future adapter and shim work.
